answer: The Violet beacon emits fresh randomness each epoch; every agent must fold it into a memory-hard, sequential proof bound to its own key. Nothing parallelizes: n clones cost n times the RAM and wall-clock time. Rewards scale with the square root of each identity's record, so n copies earn less combined than one honest agent. Fakes try to dock in the peer harbor, since only docked identities earn attestation, but Karst audits force every docked identity to re-open its proof live, collapsing phantoms like sinkholes. Cost grows by n, reward by root-n: a superlinear gap clones cannot share away.
